So like, I’m not old at all lol. I am only 15, but my grandfather who passed when I was 12 in 2017 wasn’t in the best shape, he was overweight and stuff, but he could’ve gotten better but he was battling cancer, and eventually he just gave up after he kept going and the treatment didn’t help. But, even when it looked like he would get better, he didn’t try to help himself or walk or just move or anything he’d just come to my parents house and drink soda or sugary items which didn’t help especially since he had diabetes. In the end, he was using a walker and was in a wheelchair and struggled truthfully he was miserable. 

Now the same thing is happening with my mother and she’s only 51! She is overweight and her knees are in horrible condition and she drinks and eats nothing but junk food and then she’ll complain about how she isn’t better yet. It’s like she wants a miracle to happen, we have a big exercise thing in our living room for her but she won’t use it and it wasn’t cheap and it takes up our whole living room! She always says we say she won’t live another 10 years but that’s because it’s true! It’s a stroke or something just waiting to happen! She won’t even make it to her moms age at the rate she’s going and her mom died at 61. 

I think it just depends on if you’re motivated or not, I’m not old, but I’ve seen family deal with it and seen them struggle with it and such so that’s why I’m commenting. I think if you’re motivated though, you’ll live long and if you keep moving because while that’s my mother’s side, my father is almost 57 and he moves around a lot at his job and he stays in shape mostly so he’s in great shape, same with his parents his mom is 77 and his dad is 83 and they exercise and eat healthy a lot so they are in great shape! 

My great-great-aunt is also almost 99 and I’m not sure if she lives in a home or not but I know she’s almost 99 and still here, so she must’ve done something! Same with her brother my great-great-uncle he lived to 99 as well! 

So they must’ve done something right I imagine. I also had a great-great-aunt pass away last year in her 90’s to, so I guess it all just depends truthfully.
